## Natural history notes

A medium-sized bee fly characterized by its fuzzy body, long straight proboscis, and dark wings marked with pale, sinuous clear patches that give the species its name. In Florida, it is found in sunny open habitats such as fields, roadsides, forest edges, pine flatwoods, scrub, and sandy areas where flowers and host insects are available. Adults visit flowers for nectar, while the larvae are parasitoids of other insects, developing on or in immature hosts and helping regulate populations of other arthropods.
